definition: Deciding whether two sentences express the same meaning despite different wording.
details: Deciding whether two sentences express the same meaning despite different wording. Benchmarks such as Quora Question Pairs train classifiers that feed deduplication, FAQ matching, and semantic search.

explainer.lead: Paraphrase identification decides whether two sentences express the same meaning despite different wording. It matters because it underpins deduplication, FAQ matching, and semantic search.

tiers.eli5: It's like checking whether two differently worded questions are really asking the same thing.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train classifiers on benchmark pairs such as Quora Question Pairs and deploy them to merge duplicate content or match questions to answers. A pitfall is that surface overlap misleads models, so pairs sharing many words but differing in meaning must be handled carefully.
tiers.paperLevel: Paraphrase identification is the task of deciding whether two sentences express the same meaning despite different wording; benchmarks such as Quora Question Pairs train classifiers that feed deduplication, FAQ matching, and semantic search.

explainer.example: The pair "How do I reset my password?" and "What's the way to change my password?" is labeled as a paraphrase and used to match a user to an existing FAQ entry.
